purpose: Six-coordinate effective ionic radii, for Kapustinskii lattice energies.
source: R. D. Shannon, Acta Cryst. (1976) A32, 751-767, Table 1.
quantity: 'IR' -- Shannon's EFFECTIVE ionic radius, not the 'CR' crystal radius in the adjacent column. The two differ by 0.14 A and the sign of that offset FLIPS between cations and anions, so reading the wrong column is not a constant error.
coordination: VI for every entry, and that is not a simplification of the table -- Kapustinskii's equation is DEFINED on six-coordinate radii whatever the real structure's coordination is. An entry here for any other CN would be a bug waiting to be used.
how_these_were_checked: Each value was read from a rendered image of Table 1 in the PDF (its text layer is OCR and mangles the ion labels: 'AC?3', 'AG?I'), and independently cross-checked against the `mendeleev` package's transcription of the same table. All 15 agreed exactly. mendeleev is a DEV cross-check only and is not a runtime dependency -- the values live here so the app carries its own data.
the_trap_this_avoids: Cs+ is CR 1.81 / IR 1.67 and Cl- is CR 1.67 / IR 1.81 -- the same two numbers, swapped. A spot-check that happened to land on either one would look right with the columns transposed.
extending_this: Add an ion by reading Table 1 for its VI row and taking the SECOND number. Record the charge, because a radius without one is meaningless.

crystal_radii_for_reference.comment: NOT used by any calculation. Kept so that a future reader can tell at a glance which column was taken, which is the one mistake this file exists to prevent.
